text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone on the team. One key habit is following good naming conventions. Choose clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so others can quickly see what they do. Another useful practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because bugs are simpler to find and fix. In short, writing clean code may take more effort at first, but it pays off in the long run.
